branch: the Read range suffix .t-sfx is one unbreakable token: it must never wrap internally, however crowded the line — the path beside it is the flexible part (middle-ellipsis)
provenance: Pure CSS/DOM geometry — no wire frames, so this fixture asserts only what the STYLESHEET and the tool-line builders must produce, never anything about the CLI (fixture 51's precedent, and the same defect class as its step 2: a span with no nowrap inside the tool-line flex row shrinks to min-content and wraps at its internal break points). User screenshot 2026-09-05 (Windows office box, real IDE): 'Read H:\Projects\AAA CLAUDE\...\acf-rest-values.php' with the suffix broken after the hyphen into '(lines 1-' / '150)'. REPRODUCED in the real JCEF panel 2026-09-05 pre-fix at 730px with the same builders this fixture uses (toolLine + fillPath + a .t-sfx span, the exact shape 75-retraction and 55-replay build): suffix rect 37px against a 19px line-height, computed white-space 'normal'. The long path is what crowds the line — fillPath's middle-ellipsis lets the path shrink, and flexbox then also shrinks the un-protected suffix span to its min-content, which is where the internal wrap comes from. Fix is one declaration pair on .tool-line .t-sfx (webview/css/30-blocks.css): white-space nowrap + flex 0 0 auto, so the suffix's min-content becomes its whole text and the PATH absorbs all the shrink, exactly the division of labour the tool line already promises. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN 2026-09-05 against the pre-fix build (sandbox launched before the CSS edit): both DISCRIMINATING asserts FAILED (oneLine false at 37px, nowrap 'normal'); the GUARD (path still ellipsises rather than overflowing the panel) passed both phases. Green after the edit and a sandbox restart.
